description:
forkMonitor carries the exact latent bug US-R1-001 just fixed: `const mainScript = process.argv[1] ?? 'cam'` produces [execPath, '/$bunfs/root/<outfile>', 'retry-monitor', ...] inside a compiled binary, and the child's main() reads argv[2] = the bunfs path and exits 1 with 'unknown command'. Verified with a real compiled binary from this branch: `<bin> '/$bunfs/root/<outfile>' <cmd>` prints 'unknown command'. This means `cam retry`'s monitor child is silently dead on every installed (compiled) binary. Pre-existing on main and correctly out of scope for this PR (the round-1 finding named only the orch-resolve call site, and patterns.md documents it as a follow-up target), so it is not a regression here: file it as its own issue and reuse the new exported resolveOrchResolverCmd there.

Source: cam/issue-425
Review round: 2

suggestion-fingerprint: 1085d5c932a6

---

resolveOrchResolverCmd's second detection arm, `basename(execPath) !== 'bun'`, misclassifies an interpreted run under a non-standard interpreter filename (e.g. a version-managed `bun-1.3` shim) as compiled mode, emitting `<bun-shim> orch-resolve`, which bun would treat as a script path and fail. The failure is fail-safe (fallback + one orch-resolve-fallback event per respawn, never a broken session) but silently disables live re-resolution. The bunfs-prefix arm alone is the positive signal; consider keying on it (or on Bun.main starting with '/$bunfs/') and dropping the negative basename heuristic.

Source: cam/issue-425
Review round: 2
